questions.question: What kinds of roles are you targeting? Include titles, seniority, and areas of computer science or software engineering.
What work do you most want to do? What kinds of problems, systems, or users interest you?
What work or environments do you want to avoid?
What are your strongest 3–5 professional qualities? For each, give a brief example that demonstrates it.
What do you want an employer to remember about you after reading your application?

Which 3–5 accomplishments from your experience best represent your strengths? For each, note your contribution and the result; refer the agent to your master resume or role/project questionnaires for details.
What technical strengths do you want highlighted? For each, give evidence of how you’ve used it.
What nontechnical strengths are relevant to your work—such as communication, initiative, mentoring, or handling ambiguity? Give an example for each.
What kind of teammate are you? Describe how you collaborate, give or receive feedback, and handle disagreements.
What is one example of a challenge, setback, or mistake that changed how you work? What did you learn?
What genuinely motivates you about software or computer science?
What types of products, industries, users, or technical challenges are especially meaningful to you? Why?
Are there causes, values, or mission areas you care about? Which ones, and how do they relate to your work?
What would make a role a good fit for you beyond the job title?
What claims about your interests or motivations would feel inaccurate or too strong?
What location, work arrangement, or relocation preferences should the agent know?
Are there employment, education, or career-transition details that need brief context? State what may be shared and how you’d like it phrased.
Are there gaps, changes, or constraints the agent should not explain or mention unless specifically asked?
What contact details, links, or sign-off should appear?
Are there any topics the agent must never disclose or include?
What tone should the letters use—for example, direct, warm, formal, or conversational?
What length do you prefer?
Do you want a conventional letter format, or a shorter email-style letter?
What phrases, clichés, or styles should the agent avoid?
Should the agent mention salary, availability, work authorization, or other practical matters? Specify when, if ever.
What should the agent do when the job description doesn’t provide enough company-specific information to write a sincere, tailored opening?
